subject: Order Schedule errata — clarifying ceiling exceptions & packaging mapping
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acerohealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: AceroHealth Procurement <procure@acerohealth.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order schedule inconsistency — ceiling/floor exceptions

Hi Hannah,

We were reviewing the order schedule (Exhibit B) against our internal SKU mapping and noticed what looks like an errata: Section 2.3 lists a per-sku ceiling for packaged bundles, but the packaging mapping table in Appendix A appears to exclude those same SKUs from the ceiling calculation. Practically, this means our projected spend could either hit the "ceiling" or be treated as exempt depending on which table we follow.

Can you confirm Redwood's intended interpretation here? Specifically: does the ceiling/floor carveout apply at the bundle level or the individual SKU level for mixed-package purchases? Also, are there any operational tolerances (e.g., 10% variance) that would prevent a clawback for a single quarter where mappings flip?

We're attaching our pricing_workbook.xlsx with the sample mapping that demonstrated the discrepancy. Procurement flagged this as material to committing to the Q2 ramp. Appreciate a quick confirmation and whether Redwood can provide a short redline or errata note.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Sourcing Manager — AceroHealth

Attachment: pricing_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet, 72KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acerohealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order schedule inconsistency — ceiling/floor exceptions

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and for sending the workbook. Quick summary up front: our intent was that the ceiling/floor mechanics apply at the package level (bundle), not individual SKUs, but the appendix language is ambiguous and I agree it can be read the other way.

Actionable next steps I propose:
- I'll run this past Legal for a concise errata (one-page clarifying addendum) and return a redline by EOD.
- For Q2 we can offer a one-quarter operational tolerance: if this mapping variance causes a discrepancy <= 12% vs the committed band we will not trigger a retroactive clawback for that quarter.
- Jordan / Karthik: can you review the attached annotated_exhibit_b.docx and confirm Legal & Ops are comfortable with the tolerance and the proposed wording?

If that set works for you, once Legal approves we'll share a PDF redline and a DocuSign link for execution.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Commercial Operations — Redwood Inference

Attachment: annotated_exhibit_b.docx (docx, 38KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Order schedule inconsistency — legal redline suggestion

Hannah — forwarding my suggested language below. I redlined the order form (attached) to: (1) explicitly state "package-level" as the unit of measurement for Exhibit B ceilings/floors, (2) add a single-quarter tolerance carveout (12%), and (3) include a short operational note mapping how SKUs are assigned to bundles when there's ambiguity.

Quoted for context:
> On Thu, 22 Mar 2028 at 09:12, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acerohealth.com> wrote:
> > ...

Suggested clause (ready for insertion into Exhibit B):
"For clarity, all references to 'ceiling' and 'floor' in Exhibit B shall be applied at the package (bundle) level as defined in Appendix A. Where an individual SKU could reasonably be assigned to more than one package under Appendix A, Parties shall mutually agree on package assignment in good faith. In the event the parties cannot agree within thirty (30) days, the Company (Redwood) will apply the package assignment used for invoicing and provide an operational mapping to the Customer.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Parties agree that for the first applicable quarter following execution of this amendment, Redwood will waive any retrospective clawback that would arise solely as a result of SKU-to-package mapping variance that results in a variance not exceeding twelve percent (12%) of the committed band for that quarter.
"

Attachment: redlined_orderform.pdf (pdf, 95KB)

Jordan Blake
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

P.S. Ops: Karthik — confirm we can produce the mapping export/manifest for Acero within 7 business days if needed.

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acerohealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: AceroHealth Procurement <procure@acerohealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order schedule inconsistency — ceiling/floor exceptions

Hannah / Jordan — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the proposed language. A couple of operational clarifications from our side before we sign: 

1) "Invoice assignment" as the tiebreaker could be problematic if our ERP maps SKUs differently across POs. Can Redwood commit to providing a monthly "packaging manifest" with the invoice that details SKU-to-package assignments for the preceding month? That will avoid back-and-forth after the fact.

2) The 12% tolerance is reasonable, but Procurement asks that the tolerance only be waived for true mapping variance and not for diverted usage (i.e., different product mix delivering lower seat counts). Can we add the phrase "solely as a result of SKU-to-package mapping variance" to the tolerance paragraph (I think Jordan already included this, but please confirm).

3) Can you confirm the operational lead-time: if we need to escalate mapping disagreements, what's the SLA for Redwood Ops to produce the mapping export? We need to ensure we can reconcile before the 30-day window lapses.

Attached is a short logistics_sheet.pdf that shows how our ERP currently tags bundles and SKUs.

If you can confirm the manifest cadence (monthly) and the 12% scope language, we'll route to Legal for a quick sign-off.

Regards,
Elena

Attachment: logistics_sheet.pdf (pdf, 24KB)

- Jordan has incorporated the text "solely as a result of SKU-to-package mapping variance" into the tolerance clause (see redline).
- I've uploaded the final redlined_orderform.pdf to Drive and created a DocuSign envelope for the Exhibit B errata; link below. Once signed we'll append the amendment as an exhibit to the order schedule.
